rationale: The book's core claim that 'heart of the earth' denotes Jerusalem (as navel/center of the land) draws legitimately on Ezekiel's language and the mirrored 'heart of the seas' phrase, plus some ancient extrabiblical usage, and it cleverly dissolves the three-days-and-nights counting tension by starting the clock at arrest. Yet the strongest counter (tomb/Sheol as the place of confinement) remains superior: Matthew 12:40 itself equates the phrase directly to Jonah's time inside the fish, and Jonah 2:2-6 already supplies the internal gloss equating that confinement with Sheol and 'the earth with her bars.' That reading requires no multi-step symbolic chain (sea = nations; fish = kingdom; mountains = kingdoms; belly = city center) and coheres immediately with the NT's repeated 'third-day' resurrection-from-the-dead framework. The book's elaborations, while imaginative, introduce more unsupported steps than they resolve; the common referent therefore explains the primary textual data with greater economy and fewer contradictions.
book_core_identification: Jerusalem as the navel/heart of the land (earth), so that the three days and three nights measure Jesus' time under arrest inside the city
book_secondary_elaborations: full scene-by-scene typology mapping every detail of Jonah 1–4 onto the Passion, betrayal, trial, death, resurrection and mission to the nations
great fish reidentified as a devouring kingdom (spiritually Egypt/Jerusalem riding Rome)
chronological reset that begins the three days and nights at Gethsemane/arrest rather than burial
heart of the seas = heart of the nations via the sea = peoples symbol
strongest_counter_interpretation: The grave/tomb (or more broadly Sheol/Hades, the realm of the dead) as the place of Jesus' burial and confinement between death and resurrection, directly paralleling Jonah's three days and nights inside the great fish
material_core_denial: The phrase does not primarily designate the city of Jerusalem; it designates the place of burial or the underworld where the Son of Man was confined for three days and three nights after death.
counter_case: Matthew 12:40 constructs an explicit temporal and spatial parallel between the fish's belly and the heart of the earth; the natural reading equates the two confinement locations

Jonah 2:2-6 already interprets the fish experience as 'the belly of Sheol' and 'the earth with her bars about me,' supplying the internal dictionary that equates the parallel place with the underworld/grave

The NT's repeated 'third day' resurrection formulae (Matt 16:21; Luke 24:46; 1 Cor 15:3-4) and the Acts 2:27-31 use of Psalm 16:10 locate the decisive event as deliverance from Hades/corruption, not merely exit from a city
Ephesians 4:9 and the traditional descent language reinforce a lower-parts/underworld referent without requiring redefinition of starting points or multi-layer symbols
book_explanatory_advantages: Appeals to Ezekiel 5:5 and 38:12 (Jerusalem set in the midst/navel of the land/nations) plus ancient Jewish/Christian usage of 'heart/navel of the earth' for Jerusalem
Mirrors the unique phrase 'heart of the seas' (Jonah 2:3) and thereby generates an internal parallel once 'sea = nations' is granted
Removes the classic Friday-to-Sunday counting difficulty by relocating the three days and nights to time spent inside Jerusalem from arrest onward
counter_explanatory_advantages: Requires no intermediate symbolic redefinitions; the fish-belly // heart-of-the-earth equation is stated on the surface of Matthew 12:40 itself
Jonah's own prayer already supplies the Sheol/earth-with-bars gloss, so the underworld/grave reading is text-internal rather than imported
Fits the established early-Christian and creedal pattern of death–burial–descent–resurrection without chronological special pleading
Accounts for the fact that Jonah is released from the fish onto dry land and only afterward goes to the city; the confinement itself (not the later destination) is what is timed
evidence_book_core_cannot_explain: Jonah 2:2-6's explicit equation of the fish belly with 'the belly of Sheol' and 'the earth with her bars,' which the book must reassign to a political kingdom's interior; the reassignment creates tension with the prayer's death-and-corruption language that the grave/Hades reading absorbs without remainder

The surface syntax of Matthew 12:40, which times the Son of Man's sojourn by the fish sojourn; if 'heart of the earth' is the city, the parallel confinement locations no longer match without first equating the fish itself with Jerusalem—an extra step the counter does not need
decisive_sources: Ezekiel 5:5; 38:12 (supporting color but not decisive against the Jonah parallel)
unresolved_objections: Jerusalem was indeed called the navel/heart of the earth in some Second-Temple and early Christian sources; the common reading rarely engages that data
Strictly literal 'three days and three nights' remains awkward under a Friday burial / Sunday dawn resurrection even with inclusive reckoning
